Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick responses in the RFP — a couple of clarifications from our side before we finalize the scoring. For our internal risk board we need: 

- Targeted RTO and RPO commitments for a multi-region failover (active -> standby in another region) broken down by criticality tier (critical APIs, conversational sessions, embeddings).
- Expected timeline for detection -> activation -> DNS switchover for the typical failover path (and the alternate degraded-mode fallback if full region failover isn’t possible).
- What evidence you can provide (runbooks, recent rehearsal dates and outcomes, architecture maps) — we need something to attach to the security review.

Can you confirm whether you can commit to a canary failover with us (non-prod first) and supply an evidence pack by next Thursday (2026-10-22)? Procurement will start paperwork once we have the operational commitments.

Appreciate the help,

John

John — thanks, and good to meet you (virtually). High level answers up front, then I’ll attach the evidence pack and get Grace/Vivek to confirm the technical specifics.

- Short answer on commitments: for our hosted API we operate with multi-region replication and automated failover. Typical RTO for critical APIs is 10–30 minutes depending on trigger type; RPO ranges from near-zero (for KV/prefix cache rehydration) to up to 1 minute for session state in most common configs. Embeddings and batch workloads have different windows (we’ll detail below).
- Detection -> activation -> DNS switchover: detection (internal health checks + region telemetry) ~1–3 minutes; orchestration and instance spin-up ~5–20 minutes (warm standby reduces this); DNS TTLs are customer-configurable but we recommend 30s–60s during planned failover windows.
- Evidence: I’m attaching our BCP evidence pack and a DR runbook appendix. Grace has provided a network map and a short summary of recent rehearsals.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the evidence pack now.
2) Can we schedule a non-prod canary next week (we can propose Wed/Thu) and run a short failure-scenario test (activation + smoke tests)?
3) If that goes well, procurement can proceed to DocuSign for the mutual action plan.

Looping in Grace and Vivek for confirmation on the finer points (RTO by tier, replication guarantees, and any caveats).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Stephanie — confirmed. Technical summary we can provide to Acme (short bullets for their board):

- Multi-region model: active-primary with async cross-region replication for artifacts and near-synchronous replication for KV and prefix caches where latency permits.
- RTO commitments (by tier, assuming warm standby):
  * Critical APIs (customer-facing inference endpoints, stateful routing): typical RTO 10–15 minutes. This assumes warm standby capacity pre-provisioned in the secondary region and automated orchestration enabled.
  * Standard APIs (stateless inference): typical RTO 20–30 minutes (cold start scenarios may approach upper bound).
  * Batch/embeddings: RTO depends on pipeline; for queued jobs we recommend degradations (throttling) with target RTO 1–4 hours for full recovery, but we can provide prioritized queues for critical workloads.
- RPO expectations:
  * KV/prefix cache: near-zero (milliseconds-seconds) with topology-aware replication.
  * Session state: typical RPO <= 60 seconds when session replication is enabled (we’ll document how to enable).
  * Bulk artifacts (model weights): models are pre-staged in regional caches for most supported models; when rehydration is required, add 2–10 minutes depending on model size and quantization.
- Detection and activation timeline:
  * Detection: automated health checks + cross-region telemetry: 1–3 minutes.
  * Orchestration + instance readiness: 5–20 minutes (warm standby on reserved capacity shortens this).
  * DNS switchover: recommended TTL 30–60s during a planned failover — for emergency we support shorter TTLs but recommend a staged swap to avoid cache thrash.
- Fallback tiering (graceful degradation):
  * Tier 1: Full failover to secondary region (preferred).
  * Tier 2: Degraded mode — reduced concurrency, strict response-time throttling, and fallback to cached responses for non-critical routes.
  * Tier 3: Read-only/ingest-only for non-interactive workloads; best-effort replay processing.

Attachments to include: DR-Runbook-Appendix-A.docx, network-map.png, and the rehearsal summary (included in BCP-Evidence-2026Q3.pdf). No additional NDA required for the high-level network map; if Acme wants the full topology with vendor ACLs we’ll need an NDA addendum.

Edge cases / caveats to note in the response:
- Very large model rehydrations (multi-GB) can add time; we provide model staging options and quantized variants to mitigate.
- Cold-start of autoscale pools in a full region outage will extend RTOs — we state ranges accordingly.

Happy to join the canary run and the post-mortem.

Grace
Grace Oconnor
Head of Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

John — consolidated answers and attachments below (please treat the attached pack as evidence for your security committee). Short summary you can lift into the RFP response: 

- RTO by tier (with warm standby): Critical APIs: 10–15m; Standard APIs: 20–30m; Batch/embeddings: prioritized queues 1–4h.
- RPO: KV/prefix cache near-zero; session state <=60s when replication enabled; artifact rehydration 2–10m when required.
- Detection -> activation -> DNS: 1–3m detection; 5–20m orchestration/instance readiness; 30–60s TTL DNS recommended.
- Fallback tiers: Full region failover -> degraded mode (throttling & cached responses) -> read-only/ingest-only.

Attachments included: BCP-Evidence-2026Q3.pdf (rehearsal summaries + metrics), DR-Runbook-Appendix-A.docx (play-by-play sequences), network-map.png (logical diagram). Link to the evidence pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example
